# Approval packages A and B (revised 2026-11-19). NOTHING HERE IS APPLIED OR ENABLED.

Immutable reference: the git commit that adds this file on `claude/eager-hopper-5wjvwy` (site). Files are named below; the SQL text is the committed file, not a copy.

## A. Two separate change groups
**A2 (independent, replaces a function):** `docs/subscriber-zip-health-core-revision.apply.sql` / `.rollback.sql`, generated by `scripts/build-subscriber-zip-health-revision.py` (`--check` proves the committed outputs equal the generator). Replaces `_hs_subscriber_zip_health_core()`; same signature and ACL. Fixes the map count so keys the ACTIVE N5 generation recorded as unresolved are not reported as unexplained.
- Apply guard: refuses unless the live body md5 is `3998bbf2cff02ea15f16e0ac80c03935` (the text committed in PR #3054; prior definition restored by rollback from git, not retyped). Post-condition: new body md5 `b4edac02bea49df601ca06fbfc1b547f`, ACL `{postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}`.
- Rollback: restores the prior body under the guard `new md5`, then post-condition. Function replacement only, so rollback is complete (no retained data).
- Production compatibility (read-only, no DDL): the changed CTEs were run on production; `geo.n5_generation_unresolved`, `geo.n5_generation` (state ACTIVE), `geo.n5_serving_membership` (zcta5 bpchar vs text compare handled) exist with the used columns.

**A1 (new objects only; depends on nothing in A2, over-counts N5-withheld keys until A2 is applied):** `docs/subscriber-zip-lifecycle.sql`.
- Objects: tables `subscriber_zip_lifecycle`, `_history`, `_run`; helpers `_hs_lifecycle_recon_entry_valid`, `_hs_lifecycle_recon_ok`, `_hs_subscriber_zip_stage`, `_hs_lifecycle_lock_key`; `subscriber_zip_lifecycle_sync()`; `hs_subscriber_zip_lifecycle()`.
- Owner `postgres`; `search_path = pg_catalog, public`, every reference schema-qualified. RLS ON with no policy; all privileges revoked from public/anon/authenticated; service_role has SELECT only (insert/update/delete/truncate revoked). Only `hs_subscriber_zip_lifecycle()` is granted (authenticated), takes NO ZIP argument, and checks `dashboard_admins` itself, so a caller cannot supply a ZIP or read another's data. Owner bypasses RLS (needed so the SECURITY DEFINER sync can write); non-owner roles are denied by RLS and grants.
- The sync reads `bsky_maps_priority_classification`, the Tab 2 core and its own tables. It writes only the three lifecycle tables. It cannot touch source records, reconciliation evidence rows elsewhere, founder overrides, posts or email (static test S2 asserts every write target; S2b is its positive control).
- Lifecycle transitions and the evidence each needs (stage is a ceiling, never completion):
  registered = subscriber class eligible; geography_validated = ZIP in registry with a boundary; coverage_audited = core payload present; source_assessed = applicable sources enumerated; remediation = findings other than UNVERIFIED present; **reconciliation** = only when `_hs_lifecycle_recon_ok` holds: `coverage_declared_complete` AND every applicable source has an entry with complete=true, missing=0, undecidable=0, run_id, kind verified_*, age <= 168 h. A reconciliation row alone never advances the stage.
- Rollback for A1: objects are new, but they will hold audit history. Procedure: (1) `cron.unschedule` (none exists yet); (2) export `subscriber_zip_lifecycle_history` and `_run` if kept; (3) drop in dependency order: functions, then `_run`, `_history`, `subscriber_zip_lifecycle`. If audit history must be retained, stop at step 1 and revoke the function grants instead.
- Tests: disposable Postgres 16, 52 rows PASS / 0 FAIL, including unauthorized callers (anon, authenticated non-admin, service_role writes), caller-supplied ZIP rejected, RLS denial, the two-session advisory-lock test, per-ZIP error isolation. Stub tests are NOT proof of production compatibility; the production catalog and function-body checks above are.
- Apply sequence if later approved: A2, then A1; read back md5/ACL after each; run `select public.subscriber_zip_lifecycle_sync()` manually once and inspect `_run` before any cron.

## B. Daily sync (finished, tested, NOT enabled)
- Proposed job `subscriber-zip-lifecycle-sync`, command `select public.subscriber_zip_lifecycle_sync();`, once daily 11:41 UTC (after the 10-12Z N5 activation). Disable: `select cron.unschedule('subscriber-zip-lifecycle-sync');` (identify by name in `cron.job`).
- Overlap: `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` on `_hs_lifecycle_lock_key()`; a second concurrent run logs a `skipped` run row and returns (tests C1, C2).
- Failure visibility: each run writes `_run` (success/partial/failed/skipped, error text); per-ZIP failures are isolated and counted; `hs_subscriber_zip_lifecycle()` returns `last_attempt_at`, `last_attempt_status`, `last_success_at` and `failed_runs_since_last_success`, so a recent attempt cannot hide repeated failures.
- Why daily: ZIP-level coverage facts change on the 72 h sweep and the daily N5 generation; hourly adds writes without new information. New subscribers between runs: Tab 2 reads the live classification on every load and shows `unregistered_subscriber_zips` (the gap); MAPS posting priority is handled separately by ingest `bsky_maps_subscribers_first` (15 min). Resubmit B only after A1/A2 are approved.

# A2 review material (revised 2026-11-19 after the fourth review; HOLD, not applied)
**Scope: one function, `public._hs_subscriber_zip_health_core()`. No lifecycle object, table, grant or cron.**
**Revision note:** the earlier draft named the new key `withheld_by_n5_rule` and called unresolved records "withheld by design". Production data showed that was wrong (see reason codes below). The key is now `n5_unresolved` plus `n5_unresolved_by_reason`, and Tab 2 no longer treats unresolved records as healthy.
**Diff:** `docs/subscriber-zip-health-core-revision.diff` (generated from git; the full hunks are in the response that accompanied this commit). Existing: `live` selected rows; `absent` counted every key with no membership. Proposed: `live` = `select distinct p.source_key`; new CTE `unres_r` counts live keys with no membership, grouped by `reason_code` from the ACTIVE generation's `geo.n5_generation_unresolved`; `absent` excludes keys that have an unresolved row; new keys `n5_unresolved` (total) and `n5_unresolved_by_reason` (jsonb).
**Exact denominator:** distinct `source_key` from `app_projects` where `zip` = the ZIP, `record_kind='development'`, status Proposed/Approved, `submitted_at >= current_date - 120`, lat and lng not null. **Partition (non-overlapping, exhaustive):** `recent_live_records = drawn_on_map1 + drawn_on_other_zip + n5_unresolved + not_in_serving_generation`, where: drawn_on_map1 = membership in this ZIP; drawn_on_other_zip = no membership here, membership elsewhere; n5_unresolved = no membership anywhere AND an unresolved row in the ACTIVE generation; not_in_serving_generation = no membership anywhere and no unresolved row (unexplained).
**Production partition check (read-only, 2026-11-19):** 48854: 4 = 2 here + 0 elsewhere + 2 unresolved (POINT_REJECTED 2) + 0 unexplained. 64166: 10 = 2+8+0+0. 85083: 631 = 4+627+0+0. 98684: 3 = 1+2+0+0. 07001: 0 live records (no row). Partition holds for every ZIP checked.
**Unresolved reason codes (ACTIVE generation n5-national-2026-11-19, 24,137 rows = 24,137 distinct keys):** REGISTRY_IDENT_UNRESOLVED 10,422; POINT_REJECTED 4,506; NO_INTERSECTION_WITH_GENERATION_ZCTAS 3,850; GEOMETRY_INVALID 3,326; REGISTRY_HIST_UNRECOVERABLE 1,658; RECOVERY_UNSTABLE_IDENTITY 254; SOURCE_EXCLUDED 107; RECOVERY_NOT_RETURNED 14. Only SOURCE_EXCLUDED (0.4%) is an intentional exclusion; the rest are identity, geometry or placement problems.
**Global or ZIP-specific:** one row per (generation, source_key); no key has rows for more than one ZIP; no unresolved key is also a member anywhere. The entry is generation-wide for the key (its `zip` column is the source-stated ZIP), not a statement about one ZIP's map.
**Tab 2 treatment (`lib/acq-subscriber-zip-health.js`):** unresolved records with any reason other than SOURCE_EXCLUDED raise RECORDS_MISSING_FROM_MAP, naming each reason code and count, "an identity, geometry or placement problem, not an exclusion rule" (this outranks stale and partial in the roll-up, and blocks VERIFIED_*). SOURCE_EXCLUDED raises PARTIAL_COVERAGE ("intentionally excluded ... exist but are never drawn"). An unresolved total with no reason breakdown is still RECORDS_MISSING_FROM_MAP. Unexplained records raise RECORDS_MISSING_FROM_MAP. Records drawn on a neighbouring ZIP's polygon are not a failure. The card prints "N UNRESOLVED by N5 (CODE n, ...)" and never "withheld". Effect on the live fixtures: 48854's two POINT_REJECTED records now show RECORDS_MISSING_FROM_MAP instead of looking benign.
**Draft readiness:** unchanged by A2. Tab 2 only displays; it gates nothing. Subscriber MAPS drafts come from ingest's eligibility, which requires a record drawn on Map 1 (so an unresolved record is already not draft-eligible); A2 makes that visible, it does not change it.
**Full fingerprints (md5 of `pg_proc.prosrc`):** before `3998bbf2cff02ea15f16e0ac80c03935` (live, re-read 2026-11-19 21:43Z, length 5,325); after `1d95b0de88a20c343a06d395fa723bef`. File sha256: apply `e4605432a022690579f20c2c12f5545cbb5605d97bb9080677ffa3c56720210d`, rollback `3ab4f605a0e9467a04ba09ce57a6b856c3481b3f7e6e51fc4475a3e966cf24eb`.
**Apply / rollback:** unchanged mechanism: one transaction through `mcp__Supabase__apply_migration` (or `db-sql.yml` from `main`) with `docs/subscriber-zip-health-core-revision.apply.sql` (aborts unless live md5 is the before-value; asserts the after-md5 and the ACL `{postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}`), and `...rollback.sql` (aborts unless live md5 is the after-value; restores the 77fdd06 body). The function holds no state, so rollback loses nothing.
**Tests at this head:** `node test/subscriber-zip-health.test.mjs` 49/49 (partition fixture; unresolved with reason codes is not healthy; SOURCE_EXCLUDED named as intentional; neighbouring-ZIP records not a failure; unexplained is a failure; no breakdown is still not healthy; card text); generator `--check` equal; lifecycle suite 54 PASS / 0 FAIL; cache-key test passes. No DDL was run in production.
